page_subtitle: All Silo plugin APIs, documented and interactive
sec_info_desc: Read-only object with system data. Available in service.js immediately on startup. Use for logging, feature detection, or displaying version info to users.
sec_info_explain: Contains version, OS, CPU count, and the plugin's own ID. Values are populated by the core before service.js executes.
sec_web_desc: Register HTTP endpoints and serve static files. Every route must be whitelisted in info.yaml routes[]. If not listed, request is silently dropped. Supported methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, PROPFIND.
sec_web_url_desc: All plugin routes live under /plugins/<plugin_id>/. Example: registering ts.web.staticDir("/css", "css") makes files available at /plugins/example-plugin/css/. In HTML and JS files use relative paths (e.g. css/style.css, js/app.js). Never use absolute root paths like /css/style.css, they resolve to the server root, not the plugin.
sec_web_body: parsed body: JSON object, form object, or raw string
sec_web_i18n_desc: You do not need to register /i18n/* or call staticDir("/i18n", ...). The core reads your i18n/*.json files from the plugin VFS automatically at load time and merges them into the global /i18n.js.
sec_bus_desc: Publish/subscribe messaging. Plugins communicate via named topics. Topics must be declared in info.yaml events[]. Own plugin topics (plugin:<id>:*) are always allowed.
sec_storage_desc: BoltDB-backed key-value store. Keys are prefixed with <plugin_id>: so plugins never collide. Strings only, use JSON.stringify/parse for objects. Persists across restarts.
sec_http_desc: Make outbound HTTP requests. Both GET and POST supported. Useful for fetching metadata, third-party APIs, or connectivity checks. SSRF protection is handled by the core.
sec_torrent_desc: Full torrent lifecycle: add, list, get status, remove. Works with magnets or info hashes. All operations are scoped to a user (default: "owner").
sec_users_desc: Read-only access to the user list. Returns user objects with id, username, rank (0=guest, 10=user, 50=admin, 100=owner), is_banned, created_at.
sec_i18n_desc: Plugins can add translations via static i18n/<lang>.json files (loaded automatically) AND programmatically via ts.i18n.add/addMany in service.js.
i18n_dynamic_fallback: This key was not found in any translation file. i18n returned the key itself as fallback.
i18n_dynamic_found: This key was found in the translation system (added dynamically via ts.i18n.add in service.js).
sec_crypto_desc: Cryptographic primitives for hashing, key derivation, symmetric encryption, random bytes, and safe comparison of secrets. All functions are synchronous and return strings (hex or base64) for convenient use in JavaScript.
sec_crypto_why_desc: JS does not have a native byte type. Uint8Array exists but working with it is awkward. Strings are universal: hash outputs can be stored in JSON, compared with ===, sent over HTTP.
sec_crypto_when_hash: sha256 - checksums, content IDs, cache keys
sec_crypto_when_pbkdf2: pbkdf2 - derive key from password with salt
sec_crypto_when_aes: aesGcm - encrypt secrets at rest in ts.storage
sec_crypto_when_compare: constantTimeCompare - compare tokens/hashes without timing leak
sec_torrfs_desc: Read-only virtual filesystem over the user torrent library. Provides a filesystem tree (categories, torrents, nested folders, files) built from the database. Individual files can be opened as handles and streamed through res.stream.
sec_torrfs_why_title: Why a filesystem, not just torrent list?
sec_torrfs_why_desc: ts.torrent gives you torrents as flat objects. Real clients (WebDAV, FUSE, SFTP) expect a hierarchy: folders, files, paths. ts.torrfs builds that hierarchy from the database.
sec_torrfs_db_desc: The whole tree is built from bbolt. The torrent engine is not touched during list/stat, sleeping torrents stay asleep. Only ts.torrfs.open wakes the engine and creates a reader.
sec_torrfs_handle_desc: A handle is an opaque object representing an open reader. Pass it to res.stream and the core runs http.ServeContent outside the JS mutex. The handle is closed automatically after the response finishes.
sec_manifest_desc: Every plugin has an info.yaml. Think of it as a contract: fields you declare grant permission to use those APIs. Undeclared routes or events are silently denied at runtime.
manifest_id_desc: Unique identifier. URL prefix, VFS namespace, storage prefix. Lowercase, no spaces.
manifest_name_desc: Human-readable name for admin UI and plugin lists.
manifest_version_desc: Semantic version shown in admin panel.
manifest_author_desc: Author credit shown in admin panel.
manifest_entry_desc: Path to main JS file. Executed once on startup.
manifest_theme_desc_1: If true, plugin REPLACES the root page at /. Only one plugin can be theme.
manifest_icon_desc: Path to icon inside plugin's VFS. Shown in admin plugin list.
manifest_menu_desc: Sidebar navigation entries. Each: title, route, rank, icon. User sees only where user.rank >= entry.rank.
manifest_events_desc_1: Whitelist of bus topics. Use "topic:*" for wildcard. Unlisted: permission denied.
manifest_routes_desc_1: Whitelist of URL paths. Use "/path/*" for prefix matching. Unlisted: silently dropped.
